back: Mean, naive (last value), seasonal naive (value one season ago), and drift (last value plus average change).

front: When is naive the best baseline?
back: For a random walk, or when the series changes slowly and has no clear season.
y(n) + h * (y(n) - y(1)) / (n - 1). It extends the line between the first and last point.
1 - error_model / error_baseline. Positive means better than the baseline. Negative means worse.
A number alone means nothing. A baseline shows if a complex model adds value worth its cost.

front: Which baseline for hourly data with a daily cycle?
back: Seasonal naive with m = 24: use the value from the same hour yesterday.
